sections.h2: Where is the Chippewa County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is at 319 Court Street in Sault Ste. Marie, MI 49783. The state treasury directory lists the phone as 906-635-6312, the fax as 906-635-6855 and the email as rod@chippewacountymi.gov. Call ahead for counter hours, since none are posted on the land records site.

Chippewa County is in the eastern Upper Peninsula, and Sault Ste. Marie is the county seat. A seller on Drummond Island, in the Sault, or anywhere along the St. Marys River records the deed here. Mail works as well as a visit, as long as the document, the fee and the return envelope go in together.

sections.h2: How is Chippewa County organized, and who answers tax questions?
sections.html:
Chippewa County government was set up in 1826 and once reached across most of what is now the Upper Peninsula and parts of Minnesota. The Act of March 9, 1843 cut that vast area down, and today the county follows the Canadian border along the St. Marys River. Sault Ste. Marie anchors the Sault Ste. Marie micropolitan area, and Drummond Island is part of the county.

The county itself operates the jail, maintains rural roads, runs the major local courts and keeps the deed and mortgage records. Police, fire, building and zoning, tax assessment and street maintenance belong to the cities and townships. A seller with a question about an assessed value or a building permit therefore calls the local township or city office, not the register of deeds. The register of deeds answers questions about what has been recorded against the parcel.

  • Recording, indexing and copies: the Register of Deeds at 319 Court Street.
  • Assessment and local zoning: the city or township where the house sits.
  • Tax certificates for warranty-type deeds: the treasurer offices named in MCL 211.135.

sections.h2: What does a Chippewa County seller need the Register of Deeds for?
sections.html:
The sale ends at this office, because the new deed has to be recorded to enter the county's land record. The register of deeds also holds the mortgages, discharges and liens that a title company looks for when it clears your title.

The online land records system shows how deep the file goes. Its indexes start on May 16, 1865, which gives a title examiner well over a century of names to search. Sellers who inherited a Chippewa County house can use that index to find the deed that put the family on title.

  • Guests search the index free of charge.
  • Members log in with a group, user ID and password, and login charges may apply.
  • PDF copies are bought by credit card after the search.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record and copy documents in Chippewa County?
sections.html:
State law fixes the recording fee at $30.00 per document unless a charter county has adopted its own schedule. Copies cost $1.00 per page, and a certification of a recorded document is $5.00, all under MCL 600.2567.

Chippewa County land record charges drawn from the statute and the online system
ServiceChargeWhere it comes from
Recording a document$30.00, any page countMCL 600.2567(1)(a)
Extra instrument on an assignment or discharge$3.00 eachMCL 600.2567(1)(b)
Certifying a recorded document$5.00MCL 600.2567(1)(d)
Online PDF copy$1.00 per pageChippewa land records site
Online order fee$5.00 per orderChippewa land records site

Of the $30.00 fee, $5.00 goes to the register of deeds' automation fund. The statute also says the fee is due when the document is left for recording, so send payment with the deed.

sections.h2: Which Chippewa County deeds are exempt from transfer tax?
sections.html:
Several instruments are exempt from the county tax under MCL 207.505, and a few of them come up often in Chippewa County. A deed given as security, such as a mortgage, is exempt. So is a lease, and so is a deed where the stated consideration is under $100.

  • A deed from the United States, the state or a local government as grantor.
  • A deed in foreclosure, or in lieu of foreclosure, of a government-backed or government-insured loan.
  • A deed that corrects a flaw in title already vested in the grantee.
  • A deed that straightens a boundary line when no money is paid.
  • A conveyance between spouses creating or ending a tenancy by the entireties.

Everything else is taxed at 55 cents per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state. Call the register of deeds to confirm which exemption, if any, matches your deed.

sections.h2: What goes on a Chippewa County deed besides the legal description?
sections.html:
MCL 565.201 requires details about the people on the deed, and a missing item stops the recording. Each grantee's address must be printed on the deed, with the street number if street numbers are used where the property sits and a post office address if not.

The first five digits of any Social Security number must be removed or obscured. A deed in a foreign language needs an attached English translation. An instrument signed after January 1, 1964 must show the name and business address of whoever drafted it. If a notary signed the deed, the notary's printed name belongs on the same page, near the signature.

sections.h2: Do I need a tax certificate to record a Chippewa County deed?
sections.html:
For most warranty-type deeds, yes. MCL 211.135 tells the register of deeds to require certification that the property has no unpaid taxes for the five years before the deed date, plus a statement of any tax liens or tax titles on the parcel.

The county treasurer and the local city, village or township treasurer supply those certificates. Quitclaim deeds with no warranty covenants, sheriff's deeds, and tax deeds from the state treasurer are among the exceptions. A violation by a register of deeds is a misdemeanor with a fine of up to $100, which is why the office will not skip the step.

sections.h2: What does the Chippewa County housing market look like for sellers?
sections.html:
Chippewa County is the second largest county in Michigan by land area, at 1,558 square miles of land and 2,698 square miles in total. It has shorelines on both Lake Huron and Lake Superior, and Census data show only 23.6 people per square mile.

The 2025 population estimate is 36,081, down 1.9% from the 2020 base. Owners occupy 75.0% of homes, and renters pay a median gross rent of $797. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $161,900 and the median household income is $62,217. Of the county's 20,556 housing units, 86 permits were issued in 2025. At the 2020 count, 31.7% of housing units were vacant, and the share of rented homes was 27.5%.

faqs.q: How much does Chippewa County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The state fee is $30.00 per document regardless of page count, under MCL 600.2567. Add transfer tax if it applies and any tax certification fee the treasurer charges. Ask the office at 906-635-6312 for the final total.

faqs.q: Can I search Chippewa County land records for free?
faqs.a: Yes. The online land records system lets guests search the index at no charge. Buying a PDF of a document costs $1.00 per page plus a $5.00 online fee per order, paid by credit card.

faqs.q: How far back do the Chippewa County records go?
faqs.a: The online indexes begin May 16, 1865. The system posts its own index range and upload date on its welcome screen, so you can see how current it is before you search.

faqs.q: Is a mortgage subject to transfer tax in Chippewa County?
faqs.a: No. MCL 207.505 exempts instruments given as security, and an assignment or discharge of them. You pay the recording fee, but not the transfer tax, when you record a mortgage.

faqs.q: Who do I contact about a Chippewa County deed problem?
faqs.a: Contact the Register of Deeds at 319 Court Street in Sault Ste. Marie, phone 906-635-6312, email rod@chippewacountymi.gov. For legal questions about the deed itself, hire an attorney or a title company.
